private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate matched Birchwood Hale’s and exceeded Calder Rowe’s $325; we received 498 hours and earned approximately $74,690. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how hours respond to rate changes.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to test whether the additional margin outweighs any loss of hours. Compare next quarter’s hours and published rates before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: At $350 in Q1, we received 498 hours and earned about $74,690. Arden & Cole also charged $350; Calder Rowe charged $325. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how strongly hours respond to price.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest reduction to $340 to learn whether additional hours offset the narrower margin. Reassess using next quarter's allocation and published rate card, focusing on long-run profit rather than market share alone.

private_notes.observations: At $325, below both competitors' $350 rates, we received 821 hours and earned approximately $102,619. There is not yet enough data to estimate how Meridian's allocation responds to rate changes.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly while remaining below both competitors. Compare the resulting hours and published rates next quarter to assess whether the additional margin offsets any loss of volume.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $350 to $360 coincided with hours falling from 498 to 451 and quarterly profit declining from about $74,690 to $72,186. Both competitors charged $340 in Q2.
private_notes.plan: Match the competitors’ latest published rate to test whether a larger allocation offsets the lower margin. Review hours and the next rate card before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $340 in Q2, profit rose to about $94,228 from $74,690 at $350 in Q1. Hours increased from 498 to 673, but competitors also changed rates, so the effect of our own reduction is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340 to preserve the stronger observed margin-and-volume combination. Reassess after another quarter of allocation data rather than assuming the Q2 gain was entirely caused by our rate cut.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q1, Calder Rowe received 821 hours and earned about $102,619. At $340 in Q2, hours fell to 673 and profit to about $94,228; one competitor also charged $340. The higher margin did not offset the lower volume.
private_notes.plan: Set a modestly lower rate to regain hours while preserving a substantial margin. Compare Q3 volume and profit with prior quarters before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Lowering our rate from $360 in Q2 to $340 in Q3 coincided with an increase from 451 to 568 allocated hours and higher quarterly profit. The latest competing rates were $340 and $330; the allocation formula remains unknown.
private_notes.plan: Set $330 to test whether matching the lowest published competitor rate increases hours enough to offset the $10 reduction in margin. Reassess profit and the new panel rate card next quarter rather than assuming lower rates always help.

private_notes.observations: At $340, allocated hours were 673 in Q2 and 568 in Q3 as competing rates fell. Q2 produced the highest quarterly profit so far; allocation varies enough that the effect of a small rate change remains uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest cut to $330, matching Calder Rowe's latest published rate. To exceed Q3's profit at this margin, we need roughly 612 hours. Compare the resulting allocation and profit before deciding whether to retain or reverse the cut.

private_notes.observations: Q3’s $330 rate produced 693 hours and about $90,151 in profit, below both earlier quarters. Q1’s $325 rate produced the highest profit, though competing rates were also higher then.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate moderately to improve our share of hours without sacrificing too much margin. Review whether the additional hours offset the lower margin next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Q3 produced the highest quarterly profit ($79,487) at a $340 rate. Lowering to $330 in Q4 increased hours only slightly (568 to 577) and reduced profit to $74,971, though competing rates also fell.
private_notes.plan: Return to $340 to test whether the higher margin outweighs any lost hours at current competitor rates. Reassess after observing Q5 allocations and the new rate card.

private_notes.observations: The Q4 cut from $340 to $330 increased allocated hours only slightly, from 568 to 577 versus Q3, while quarterly profit fell from $79,487 to $74,971. Competitor rates also fell by $10, so our relative pricing did not improve.
private_notes.plan: Restore the $340 rate. At recent allocation levels, the higher margin should outweigh a modest loss of hours. Reassess after seeing Q5 hours and the new panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: Lowering our rate from $340 in Q2 to $320 in Q4 increased allocated hours only modestly, while quarterly profit fell from $94,228 to $84,526. Competitors’ published rates have also declined.

private_notes.observations: At $340 in Q5, Arden & Cole received 606 hours and earned approximately $84,818, its strongest quarter so far. The $350 and $360 rates produced lower profits, while $330 did not generate enough additional hours to offset its lower margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340 to preserve the strong recent combination of margin and allocated hours. Reassess if the next rate card or allocation changes materially.

private_notes.observations: At $340, quarterly profits have ranged from $79,487 to $94,228; Q5 profit was $84,818. The $330 quarter earned $74,971, and the $350 quarter earned $74,690. Recent panel rates have converged near $340.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340. The observed additional hours at $330 have not compensated for its lower margin, while $350 produced lower profit. Reassess as further allocations reveal demand.

private_notes.observations: At $340 in Q5, hours fell to 606 and profit to $84,818. The earlier $325 rate produced our highest quarterly profit, though demand may have changed since Q1. Recent lower rates have not consistently restored hours.
private_notes.plan: Set $325 to test whether a meaningful discount to the other firms' recent $340 rates restores enough hours to offset the lower margin. Reassess using Q6 hours and the new panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $340, quarterly profit was $79,487, $84,818, and $76,690. The lower Q6 allocation coincided with Calder Rowe reducing its rate to $325, but $340 remains our best-tested rate.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $340. Monitor whether the Q6 reduction in hours persists before changing the rate.

private_notes.observations: At $340, quarterly profit has ranged from about $76,690 to $94,228. The observed $330 and $350 quarters both earned less, though allocation also varies with other factors.

private_notes.observations: At $340, quarterly profit has ranged from about $76,690 to $94,228. The limited history does not establish that changing the rate would improve profit; $330 and $350 each produced lower observed profit.

private_notes.observations: At $340, the last three quarters each yielded 548 hours and $76,690 profit. Historical outcomes do not establish that a different rate would improve long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: At $295 in Q17, with competitors at $340 and $290, we received 759 hours and earned $72,128. Earlier $325 rates were more profitable when both competitors charged around $340, but profit fell when a competitor cut its rate.

Raising our rate to $340 when rivals charged $290 and $295 sharply reduced our hours and profit. A deep cut to $274 previously raised hours substantially, but its profit advantage may not persist at today's lower rival rates.
